node.title: Unmarked straightening as a Quillen equivalence for simplicial correspondences
node.statement:
Use simplicial sets, Kan complexes and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], small simplicial categories of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting], the coherent realization $\mathfrak C$ and the cosimplicial simplicial sets $Q^n=\mathfrak C[(\Delta^n\star\{y\})\amalg_{\Delta^n}\{x\}](x,y)$ of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching], the Kan model structure (including Kan fibrations) of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], and the contravariant model structure and model-generation conventions of [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model]. Fix a small simplicial set $S$, a small simplicial category $D$, and a simplicial functor $\phi:\mathfrak C[S]\to D^{\mathrm{op}}$. For $a:X\to S$ let $v$ be a new vertex and put $M_{a,\phi}=\mathfrak C[X\star\Delta^0]\amalg_{\mathfrak C[X]}D^{\mathrm{op}}$, using $\phi\mathfrak C[a]$ as the second attaching map; the join is the ordered cone with its last vertex $v$. Define $L_\phi(X)(d)=M_{a,\phi}(d,v)$, with the $D$-action given by precomposition. Define the simplicial set $U_\phi(F)$ over $S$ by declaring that its $n$-simplices over $\sigma:\Delta^n\to S$ are enriched natural transformations $L_\phi(\Delta^n\xrightarrow{\sigma}S)\to F$. Operators are restriction along simplex operators. Here an enriched natural transformation has simplicial maps at objects satisfying the action-square equality.

The category of simplicial functors $D\to\mathrm{sSet}$ and enriched natural transformations has a cofibrantly generated projective model structure with functorial factorizations: weak equivalences and fibrations are respectively objectwise weak homotopy equivalences and objectwise Kan fibrations, and cofibrations are maps with the left lifting property against the objectwise trivial fibrations. The displayed constructions are an adjunction $L_\phi\dashv U_\phi$; $L_\phi$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. If $\phi$ induces weak homotopy equivalences on every mapping simplicial set and an equivalence on the categories obtained by taking components of mapping simplicial sets, this adjunction is a Quillen equivalence: for every $X\to S$ and every projectively fibrant $F$, a map $L_\phi X\to F$ is a projective weak equivalence if and only if its adjoint $X\to U_\phi F$ is a contravariant weak equivalence. Moreover $U_\phi F\to S$ is a right fibration whenever $F$ is projectively fibrant.

For every $F$ and $s\in S_0$ there is a natural simplicial isomorphism $(U_\phi F)_s\cong\operatorname{Sing}_Q(F(\phi(s)))$, where $\operatorname{Sing}_Q(T)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(Q^n,T)$. Under this isomorphism the restriction to a fiber of an adjoint map $X\to U_\phi F$ is adjoint to the composite $|X_s|_Q\to(L_\phi X)(\phi(s))\to F(\phi(s))$; for every simplicial set $K$, define $|K|_Q=\int^{[n]}K_n\times Q^n$ as the quotient of $\coprod_nK_n\times Q^n$ by $(K(\alpha)(z),q)\sim(z,Q(\alpha)(q))$ for $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, $z\in K_n$ and $q\in Q^m$. The first arrow of that composite is induced by the fiber inclusion into the ordered cone. Here trivial means also a weak equivalence, and projectively fibrant means that every value is a Kan complex. No quasicategory assumption on $S$ or local Kan assumption on $D$ is made.

node.title: Projective simplicial-presheaf model structure and its generators
node.statement:
Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$; small means $\mathcal U$-small and all categories under discussion fit in $\mathcal U'$. Use the simplicial sets of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], and model and simplicial-model terminology as defined in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. The Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] is left proper, combinatorial, and simplicial for its usual Cartesian enrichment. Here left proper means that pushing out a weak equivalence along a cofibration preserves weak equivalences; combinatorial means locally presentable with small generating sets for the two weak factorization systems, and locally presentable means generated under $\kappa$-filtered colimits, for a regular $\kappa$, by a small set of objects whose Hom functors preserve these colimits.

For every small ordinary category $D$, the category $\mathsf U(D)=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{sSet})$ has a functorial left proper combinatorial simplicial projective model structure with objectwise weak homotopy equivalences and objectwise Kan fibrations. Its cofibrations have the left lifting property against the objectwise trivial fibrations and are objectwise monomorphisms. Generating cofibrations and generating trivial cofibrations are respectively
$$h_d\times\partial\Delta^n\longrightarrow h_d\times\Delta^n,\qquad h_d\times\Lambda_i^n\longrightarrow h_d\times\Delta^n,$$
where $h_d(e)=\operatorname{Hom}_D(e,d)$ is regarded as a discrete simplicial set, $n\geq0$ in the first family and $n\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq n$ in the second. Its tensor and cotensor by a simplicial set are objectwise; its enriched mapping simplicial set has $n$-simplices the natural maps $F\times\Delta^n\to G$. Its fibrant objects are exactly the presheaves of Kan complexes. No finiteness or nonemptiness condition on $D$ is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-presheaf-local-presentability] first with $C=\Delta$, $\mathcal A=\mathsf{Set}$, and then with $C=D$, $\mathcal A=\mathsf{sSet}$. This gives local presentability of simplicial sets and of $\mathsf U(D)$. Simplicial sets have pullbacks and all small limits and colimits by taking the corresponding sets in every simplicial degree; the simplicial operators are induced by the universal properties. The same objectwise construction gives all small limits and colimits of $\mathsf U(D)$. It works for every small $D$, including the empty category.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], the Kan model structure has monomorphism cofibrations, the boundary generating cofibrations and horn generating trivial cofibrations, and Kan complexes as fibrant objects. Every object is cofibrant since $\varnothing\to X$ is degreewise injective. Apply [lem-coef-all-cofibrant-left-proper] to obtain left properness. Together with Step 1 and the two small generating families, this proves combinatoriality. For the Cartesian enrichment put $\operatorname{Map}(X,Y)_n=\operatorname{Hom}(X\times\Delta^n,Y)$, tensor $X\times K$ and cotensor $Y^K$, where $(Y^K)_n=\operatorname{Hom}(K\times\Delta^n,Y)$ and simplicial operators act by precomposition. The adjunction is explicit: a map $X\times K\to Y$ sends a simplex $x:\Delta^n\to X$ to the composite $\Delta^n\times K\to X\times K\to Y$; the inverse evaluates this family on the identity simplex, and naturality makes the two formulas inverse. For monomorphisms $i,j$, their pushout product is the inclusion of the union of $B\times C$ and $A\times E$ in $B\times E$, hence is monic. If either factor is trivial, it is anodyne by [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product], using symmetry when necessary; anodyne equals trivial cofibration by the Kan lifting system. Exponential adjunction identifies a horn lifting problem for the mapping-space map associated to $i,p$ with a lifting problem for $i\mathbin\square(\Lambda_k^n\to\Delta^n)$ against $p$, and identifies boundary lifting similarly. The pushout-product conclusions therefore give exactly the simplicial model axiom, including both triviality alternatives.

proof.text: For each $d\in D$ define $L_d(K)(e)=\coprod_{\alpha:e\to d}K=h_d(e)\times K$, with restriction along $\beta:e^{\prime}\to e$ sending $(\alpha,x)$ to $(\alpha\beta,x)$. Evaluation at the identity of $d$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(L_dK,F)=\operatorname{Hom}(K,F(d))$: its inverse sends $x:K\to F(d)$ to $(\alpha,k)\mapsto F(\alpha)(x(k))$. The two formulas are inverse by naturality at $\alpha$ and at $1_d$. Thus $L_d$ is left adjoint to evaluation, and lifting squares correspond under these same formulas. Let $I_D$ and $J_D$ be $L_d$ applied to all boundary and horn inclusions with the ranges in the statement. These are small sets since $D$ is small. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], $I_D^{\square}$ is exactly the objectwise trivial fibrations and $J_D^{\square}$ exactly the objectwise Kan fibrations.

proof.text: Run the cellular small object argument separately on $I_D$ and $J_D$. Its smallness hypothesis is justified as follows. By Step 1 and [lem-coef-object-presentability-rank], each domain of a generator has a regular presentability rank. The domains form a small family. Apply [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound] to the underlying sets of these rank cardinals and choose an infinite regular $\lambda$ greater than all of them. The initial ordinal of $\lambda$ is filtered for every smaller rank, so the Hom functor of each domain preserves every continuous $\lambda$-chain, in particular chains of generator-cell attachments. The hypotheses of [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization] now hold. It gives functorial factorizations into an $I_D$-cell map followed by an objectwise trivial fibration, and into a $J_D$-cell map followed by an objectwise fibration. It also identifies each generated left lifting class with the arrow retracts of the corresponding cell maps.

source.place: Proof of Proposition A.2.8.2, the two small-object factorizations; cited cardinal and cellular lemmas discharge the smallness hypothesis. Read online; not archived in literature/. The detailed assembly is by the worker.

proof.text: Define weak equivalences objectwise, fibrations as $J_D^{\square}$, and cofibrations as ${}^{\square}(I_D^{\square})$. Evaluation preserves colimits by their explicit objectwise construction. An evaluated $I_D$ generator is a coproduct of boundary inclusions, so every $I_D$-cell map is objectwise monic, as are its arrow retracts. An evaluated $J_D$ generator is a coproduct of trivial Kan cofibrations. A cell composite built from these has the left lifting property against every Kan fibration: solve a square at each attached summand, extend the chosen diagonal at successor stages, and use the colimit universal property at limit stages. Retracts inherit the diagonal by composing the retract maps. Hence every $J_D$-cell map is an objectwise trivial cofibration, in particular a weak equivalence, and is a projective cofibration since its generators lift against objectwise trivial fibrations. Conversely, if a projective cofibration $f$ is an objectwise weak equivalence, factor $f=pj$ by the $J_D$ factorization of Step 4. Both $j$ and $f$ are objectwise weak equivalences, so $p$ is an objectwise trivial fibration. A lift against $p$ makes $f$ an arrow retract of $j$ (the retract has identity on the source and the diagonal on the target). Therefore the second generated left class is precisely the trivial projective cofibrations. The two weak factorization systems now satisfy all the model axioms: retract and two-out-of-three for weak equivalences are componentwise, and completeness, cocompleteness and functorial factorizations were proved above. This also proves exactly the asserted two generating families, objectwise monomorphism property, and combinatoriality.

proof.text: Define $(F\otimes K)(d)=F(d)\times K$ and $(G^K)(d)=G(d)^K$, using at each object the Cartesian cotensor of Step 2, and put $\operatorname{Map}(F,G)_n=\operatorname{Nat}(F\times\Delta^n,G)$; a simplicial operator acts by precomposition on $\Delta^n$, and composition is pointwise using the diagonal of $\Delta^n$. The objectwise exponential adjunction of Step 2 is natural in $d$, so it restricts to natural families and gives bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(F\otimes K,G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,\operatorname{Map}(F,G))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,G^K)$, natural in all three variables: a natural family $F(d)\times K\to G(d)$ sends a simplex $k:\Delta^n\to K$ to the composite $F\times\Delta^n\to F\times K\to G$, and conversely a map $K\to\operatorname{Map}(F,G)$ is evaluated on the identity simplices. Equivalently $\operatorname{Map}(F,G)$ is the equalizer of the two maps from $\prod_d\operatorname{Map}(F(d),G(d))$ to $\prod_{\alpha:e\to d}\operatorname{Map}(F(d),G(e))$; it is an end, not an objectwise mapping object. Pushout-product axiom: let $i:A\to B$ be a projective cofibration, $j:K\to L$ a monomorphism of simplicial sets and $p:X\to Y$ an objectwise Kan fibration. Write $i\mathbin\square j:(A\otimes L)\amalg_{A\otimes K}(B\otimes K)\to B\otimes L$ and $p^{\square j}:X^L\to X^K\times_{Y^K}Y^L$. Applying the natural bijections above to the corners of the squares, and the universal properties of the pushout and the pullback, commutative squares from $i\mathbin\square j$ to $p$ correspond bijectively to commutative squares from $i$ to $p^{\square j}$, and diagonal fillers correspond to diagonal fillers. Cotensors and pullbacks are objectwise, so the component of $p^{\square j}$ at $d$ is the map $\operatorname{Map}(L,X(d))\to\operatorname{Map}(K,X(d))\times_{\operatorname{Map}(K,Y(d))}\operatorname{Map}(L,Y(d))$ of Step 2 for the monomorphism $j$ and the Kan fibration $p(d)$. By Step 2 it is a Kan fibration, and a trivial fibration if $j$ or $p(d)$ is trivial. (a) If $p$ is an objectwise trivial fibration, $p^{\square j}$ is an objectwise trivial fibration, so $i$ lifts against it by definition of projective cofibrations; hence $i\mathbin\square j$ lifts against every objectwise trivial fibration and is a projective cofibration. (b) If $j$ is a weak equivalence, $p^{\square j}$ is an objectwise trivial fibration for every objectwise Kan fibration $p$, so $i\mathbin\square j$ lifts against every projective fibration, i.e. lies in ${}^{\square}(J_D^{\square})$, which is the class of trivial projective cofibrations by Step 5. (c) If $i$ is a trivial projective cofibration, then $i\in{}^{\square}(J_D^{\square})$ by Step 5 and $p^{\square j}$ is an objectwise Kan fibration, i.e. lies in $J_D^{\square}$; so $i$ lifts against it and again $i\mathbin\square j$ is a trivial projective cofibration. Finally, for a projective cofibration $i:A\to B$ and a projective fibration $p:X\to Y$, the tensor adjunction identifies a lifting problem of $\partial\Delta^n\to\Delta^n$ (resp. $\Lambda^n_k\to\Delta^n$) against $\operatorname{Map}(B,X)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,X)\times_{\operatorname{Map}(A,Y)}\operatorname{Map}(B,Y)$ with a lifting problem of $i\mathbin\square(\partial\Delta^n\to\Delta^n)$ (resp. $i\mathbin\square(\Lambda^n_k\to\Delta^n)$) against $p$. By (b) the horn case is solvable, so this map is a Kan fibration; if $p$ is trivial, (a) solves the boundary case, and if $i$ is trivial, (c) does; by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] the map is then a trivial fibration. This proves the asserted simplicial projective structure with its precise tensor, cotensor and mapping object.

proof.text: A pushout along a projective cofibration is objectwise a pushout along a Kan cofibration, by Step 5. The Kan structure is left proper by Step 2, so pushing out an objectwise weak equivalence preserves objectwise weak equivalences. Thus the projective structure is left proper. Finally, its terminal diagram is objectwise the terminal simplicial set. Its terminal map is a projective fibration exactly when every component terminal map is a Kan fibration, that is, when every component is a Kan complex by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. For empty $D$ there is one diagram and one arrow, and the empty generating families yield the terminal model category. No step required finite $D$ or a chosen object of $D$.

node.title: Projective simplicial diagram models and change of index
node.statement:
Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$; small means $\mathcal U$-small and all categories under discussion fit in $\mathcal U'$. Use simplicial model categories of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], and simplicial categories and Dwyer--Kan equivalences of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Let $\mathcal A$ be a combinatorial simplicial model category: its underlying category is generated under $\kappa$-filtered colimits, for some regular $\kappa$, by a small set of objects whose Hom functors preserve those colimits, and its two model weak factorization systems are generated by small sets. For every small simplicial category $I$, the category $\mathcal A^I$ of simplicial functors and enriched natural transformations has a combinatorial simplicial projective model structure, with objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations. Its simplicial tensor and cotensor are objectwise, and its mapping simplicial set is the enriched end of the objectwise mapping sets. Evaluation preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations, and in particular sends projectively cofibrant fibrant diagrams to cofibrant fibrant objects. The enriched free diagram left adjoint to evaluation at $i$ is $X\mapsto I(i,-)\otimes X$.

If $v:I\to J$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence of small simplicial categories, enriched left Kan extension and restriction give a simplicial Quillen equivalence $v_!: \mathcal A^I\rightleftarrows\mathcal A^J:v^*$. A Quillen equivalence here means that for cofibrant $P$ and fibrant $Q$, a map $v_!P\to Q$ is a weak equivalence exactly when its adjoint $P\to v^*Q$ is. No local Kan hypothesis on $I$ or $J$ is imposed.

source.place: Proposition A.3.3.2, Remarks A.3.3.4-A.3.3.5, Propositions A.3.3.7-A.3.3.8, printed pp.870-873, specialized to Kan-model simplicial sets. All simplicial sets are cofibrant, so the objectwise-cofibration assertion of Remark A.3.3.5 applies. Read online; not archived in literature/. proof.text:
Write $O=\operatorname{Ob}I$ and $\mathcal B=\prod_{i\in O}\mathcal A$. The product is locally presentable by [lem-coef-accessible-monad-presentability]. On it define
$$ (TX)_j=\coprod_{i\in O} I(i,j)\otimes X_i. $$
The unit inserts the identity vertex in $I(j,j)$ and the multiplication uses $I(j,k)\times I(i,j)\to I(i,k)$ and the tensor associativity. Thus the monad identities are precisely the identity and associativity identities of $I$. A $T$-algebra is exactly a family $X_i$ with unital associative action maps $I(i,j)\otimes X_i\to X_j$, hence an enriched functor; algebra morphisms are exactly enriched natural transformations. For each simplicial set $K$, $K\otimes-$ is left adjoint to $(-)^K$, by the tensor/cotensor axiom of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]; it therefore preserves colimits (apply the adjunction to the defining cocone). Coproducts also commute with colimits by their universal property. Consequently $T$ preserves all small colimits, in particular filtered colimits. Apply the accessible-monad statement to deduce that $\mathcal A^I$ is locally presentable, complete and cocomplete. Colimits in it are objectwise: the colimit of each action map exists since $I(i,j)\otimes-$ preserves that colimit, and the action identities hold after every colimit insertion. Limits are objectwise as well: the action into each limiting value is the unique map with the prescribed projections, whose action identities follow after those projections. All coproduct and product indexing sets above are small.

proof.text: For $i\in O$ define $F_iX$ by $(F_iX)_j=I(i,j)\otimes X$, with action given by composition. A transformation $F_iX\to P$ is determined by its restriction $X\to P_i$ at the identity of $i$; conversely a map $a:X\to P_i$ gives the component $I(i,j)\otimes X\xrightarrow{1\otimes a}I(i,j)\otimes P_i\to P_j$. The two constructions are inverse by the identity and composition axioms. For every $n$, tensor associativity identifies $(F_iX)\otimes\Delta^n$ with $F_i(X\otimes\Delta^n)$. The displayed inverse constructions therefore identify the $n$-simplices of $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(F_iX,P)$ with maps $X\otimes\Delta^n\to P_i$, the $n$-simplices of $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(X,P_i)$. Restriction along each simplex operator commutes with inserting the identity and with the action maps, so these bijections give an isomorphism of simplicial sets, natural in $X,P$. This proves the enriched adjunction. In particular $F_i$ preserves all small colimits. Let $S$ and $T_0$ be small generating cofibrations and generating trivial cofibrations of $\mathcal A$, and put $S_I=\{F_i(s)\}$, $T_I=\{F_i(t)\}$. A square against $F_i(s)$ or $F_i(t)$ is, under this adjunction, exactly a square against $s$ or $t$ at $i$, with the same choices of diagonal filler. Hence $S_I^{\square}$ is exactly the class of objectwise trivial fibrations and $T_I^{\square}$ exactly the class of objectwise fibrations. This uses only the specified two generating lifting systems and tensor adjunction of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization].

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent derived coefficient-adjunction foundation; HTT A.3.3.5 and A.2.8.2: free diagrams and the two right lifting classes

proof.text: For every domain $A$ of an arrow of $S_I\cup T_I$, [lem-coef-object-presentability-rank] supplies a small infinite regular $\tau_A$ for which $\operatorname{Hom}(A,-)$ preserves $\tau_A$-filtered colimits. Apply [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound] to the small family of underlying sets of these cardinals; it gives an infinite regular $\lambda$ larger than every $\tau_A$. The ordinal $\lambda$ is $\tau_A$-filtered: fewer than $\tau_A$ of its elements have an upper bound below $\lambda$ by regularity. Thus each domain Hom functor preserves colimits of $\lambda$-chains, including the continuous cellular chains required in [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization]. Apply that node separately to $S_I$ and $T_I$. It gives functorial cell-map/right-lifting factorizations and identifies each left lifting class with the arrow retracts of its cell maps. Write $C_I={}^{\square}(S_I^{\square})$ and $D_I={}^{\square}(T_I^{\square})$ for these classes. They form functorial weak factorization systems with the indicated right classes: a map right-orthogonal to the left class is right-orthogonal to its generators, and the converse follows by extending a lift over each cell and passing to retracts. The same lifting argument proves closure of either left class under small coproducts, pushouts and continuous transfinite compositions: solve on each summand, use the pushout universal property, and extend successively with the colimit lift at each limit stage. No choice of a functorial factorization is inferred from a merely existential cellular statement.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent derived coefficient-adjunction foundation; HTT A.2.8.2(i)-(iii), used in A.3.3.2: both small-object factorizations and their explicit retract argument

proof.text: Every simplicial set is cofibrant in the Kan model structure [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. The simplicial model axiom [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], applied to $\varnothing\to I(i,j)$, implies that $I(i,j)\otimes-$ sends cofibrations to cofibrations and trivial cofibrations to trivial cofibrations: indeed, a lifting square from $a\mathbin\square b$ to a coefficient fibration $p$ is, by the tensor/mapping adjunction, a lifting square from the simplicial arrow $b$ to the mapping-space arrow associated to $(a,p)$. If $a,b$ are cofibrations, the latter square lifts when $p$ is trivial; if either $a$ or $b$ is trivial, it lifts for every fibration $p$. The two coefficient lifting systems give the claimed pushout-product classes. Therefore the generators $S_I$ evaluate to cofibrations and the generators $T_I$ to trivial cofibrations. Evaluation preserves colimits by Step 1. The lifting-extension and retract arguments of Step 3, now in $\mathcal A$, show that every $C_I$ map is objectwise a cofibration and every $D_I$ map is objectwise a trivial cofibration. In particular $D_I\subseteq W_I$, where $W_I$ means objectwise weak equivalence. Since $S_I^{\square}$ is contained in $T_I^{\square}$, one also has $D_I\subseteq C_I$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent derived coefficient-adjunction foundation; HTT A.3.3.5: local cofibrancy of the indexing category and evaluation of the cellular generators

proof.text: The classes $W_I$ are retract closed and satisfy two-out-of-three, object by object, by the model axioms of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. If $f\in C_I\cap W_I$, factor it using Step 3 as $f=pj$, with $j\in D_I$ and $p$ objectwise a fibration. Step 4 gives $j\in W_I$, so $p\in W_I$ by two-out-of-three. Thus $p\in S_I^{\square}$ and the left lifting property of $f$ makes $f$ an arrow retract of $j$. It follows that $f\in D_I$. We have proved $D_I=C_I\cap W_I$, while $S_I^{\square}=T_I^{\square}\cap W_I$ is the identity already proved in Step 2. The two weak factorization systems of Step 3 are consequently exactly $(C_I,F_I\cap W_I)$ and $(C_I\cap W_I,F_I)$ with $F_I$ the objectwise fibrations. Completeness and cocompleteness were proved in Step 1. These are all the model axioms, with functorial factorizations generated by the two small displayed sets; together with local presentability they prove combinatoriality. This argument does not require cofibrant domains for the chosen generating maps.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent derived coefficient-adjunction foundation; HTT A.2.8.2 projective lifting argument, as invoked in A.3.3.2

proof.text:
Define the tensor and cotensor of diagrams pointwise, with action maps induced by tensor associativity and by its adjunction, respectively. Their mapping simplicial set is the equalizer
$$\prod_i\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(P_i,Q_i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathsf{sSet}}\bigl(I(i,j),\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(P_i,Q_j)\bigr).$$
The two arrows compose the family of maps with the actions of $P$ and $Q$. A map from a parameter $K$ to this equalizer is exactly a family $K\otimes P_i\to Q_i$ satisfying enriched naturality, which verifies the asserted tensor and cotensor adjunctions and the enriched-end description. For a generating arrow $F_i(a)$ in either $S_I$ or $T_I$ and a simplicial cofibration $b$, the pushout product is $F_i(a\mathbin\square b)$, since $F_i$ commutes with tensors and colimits. The simplicial model axiom in $\mathcal A$ makes $a\mathbin\square b$ a cofibration, trivial if $a$ or $b$ is trivial; $F_i$ preserves these two classes by Step 2's lifting adjunction. For fixed $b$, pushout product preserves pushouts, coproducts and continuous transfinite composites of arrows, as follows by writing each side as its defining colimit, and it preserves retracts by functoriality. Applying Step 3 to $S_I$ therefore proves that $c\mathbin\square b$ is a cofibration for every projective cofibration $c$, and is trivial when $b$ is trivial. Applying Step 3 separately to $T_I$ proves that $c\mathbin\square b$ is trivial for every projective trivial cofibration $c$ and every simplicial cofibration $b$. Closure of the resulting left lifting classes follows by the lift extensions in Step 3. This proves the simplicial model axiom for the actual displayed mapping sets of $\mathcal A^I$ using [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Evaluation preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations by Step 4, and fibrations by their definition. Hence a projectively cofibrant fibrant diagram has cofibrant fibrant values, since initial and terminal diagrams are pointwise initial and terminal.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent derived coefficient-adjunction foundation; HTT A.3.3.4-A.3.3.5: tensor structure, simplicial compatibility and bifibrant evaluation

proof.text:
For any simplicial functor $v:I\to J$, define
$$ (v_!P)_j=\int^{i\in I}J(vi,j)\otimes P_i. $$
Concretely this is the coequalizer of the two action maps from $\coprod_{i,i'}(J(vi',j)\times I(i,i'))\otimes P_i$ to $\coprod_iJ(vi,j)\otimes P_i$. Smallness of $I$ and cocompleteness of $\mathcal A$ guarantee its existence. The action of $J$ is induced by composition on its first tensor factor. A transformation from this coequalizer to $Q$ is exactly a family $P_i\to Q_{vi}$ compatible with the $I$-actions: in one direction restrict to the identity of $vi$, and in the other use the action $J(vi,j)\otimes Q_{vi}\to Q_j$. The coequalizer relation is precisely the compatibility needed. Tensoring this coequalizer with a parameter $K$ commutes with its coproducts and coequalizer and replaces each $P_i$ by $K\otimes P_i$. The identity-vertex and action constructions above then give inverse bijections between maps $K\otimes v_!P\to Q$ and maps $K\otimes P\to v^*Q$. Taking $K=\Delta^n$ gives bijections on every degree of the enriched mapping sets; their formulas commute with all simplex operators. Thus they give the simplicial adjunction $v_!\dashv v^*$. Restriction preserves objectwise fibrations and trivial fibrations, so its left adjoint preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations by the adjunction of lifting squares. We have a simplicial Quillen adjunction. To identify $v_!F_iX$, maps from it to any $Q$ correspond, by the two adjunctions, to maps $X\to Q_{vi}$, which correspond to maps $F_{vi}X\to Q$. These natural bijections identify $v_!F_iX$ with $F_{vi}X$, compatibly with the identity-vertex units. These arguments only use tensor adjunctions and the model lifting definitions in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization].

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent derived coefficient-adjunction foundation; HTT A.3.3.7: explicit enriched left Kan extension and its Quillen property

proof.text:
First suppose that $v$ is a DK equivalence and that every $I(i,k)\to J(vi,vk)$ is degreewise injective. Put $H=v^*v_!$ and let $\eta:1\to H$ be its unit; $H$ preserves all colimits by Step 1 and the left adjunction in Step 7. Call $a:P\to P'$ good when its relative unit
$$ r_a: HP\amalg_P P'\longrightarrow HP' $$
is objectwise a trivial cofibration. For $a=F_i(s)$, where $s:A\to B$ is a generating cofibration of $\mathcal A$, evaluation at $k$ identifies $r_a$ with
$$ (J(vi,vk)\otimes A)\amalg_{I(i,k)\otimes A}(I(i,k)\otimes B)\longrightarrow J(vi,vk)\otimes B. $$
This is the pushout product of $s$ with $I(i,k)\to J(vi,vk)$. The second factor is a weak equivalence by DK fully faithfulness and a cofibration by the extra injectivity assumption and [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. The simplicial model axiom [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] therefore makes this displayed map a trivial cofibration, without any cofibrancy requirement on $A$ or $B$. Every generating projective cofibration is good.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent derived coefficient-adjunction foundation; HTT A.3.3.8, condition (*) and the displayed pushout-product map

proof.text: The good maps of Step 8 are closed under pushout: if $a'$ is a pushout of $a$, then $r_{a'}$ is the pushout of $r_a$, because $H$ preserves pushouts. They are closed under coproducts and retracts for the same reason. To see the transfinite assertion without presuming left properness, let $(P_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\lambda}$ be a continuous sequence of good successor maps, and set $Z_\alpha=HP_\alpha\amalg_{P_\alpha}P_\lambda$. For each successor $\alpha+1$, the map $Z_\alpha\to Z_{\alpha+1}$ is a pushout of $r_{P_\alpha\to P_{\alpha+1}}$; at a limit ordinal the sequence is continuous since $H$ preserves colimits. Thus $Z_0\to Z_\lambda=HP_\lambda$ is a transfinite composite of objectwise trivial cofibrations, and it is exactly $r_{P_0\to P_\lambda}$. Such composites remain trivial cofibrations by the successive lifting construction against fibrations, with the lift at a limit supplied by the colimit. This construction uses just the weak factorization systems in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. By the cellular-retract description in Step 3 every projective cofibration is good. For a cofibrant $P$ apply this to $0\to P$: since $H0=0$, its relative unit is $\eta_P:P\to v^*v_!P$, hence this unit is an objectwise trivial cofibration.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent derived coefficient-adjunction foundation; HTT A.3.3.8: the weak saturation of good maps, with the continuous transfinite filtration written out

proof.text: Restriction along a functor essentially surjective on $\pi_0$ reflects weak equivalences between objectwise fibrant diagrams. Here is the necessary verification. For a fibrant object $Y$ of $\mathcal A$, the simplicial model axiom makes both evaluations $Y^{\Delta^1}\to Y$ trivial fibrations, because either endpoint inclusion $\Delta^0\to\Delta^1$ is a trivial Kan cofibration. Their common constant-path section is consequently a weak equivalence. In the ordinary localization of $\mathcal A$, these two evaluations have the same inverse and are equal. Thus two maps connected by a simplicial edge in their mapping set have the same localized image when their target is fibrant; a finite zigzag of edges has the same consequence. If $e:j\to j'$ is invertible in $\pi_0J$, choose a vertex representing its inverse. Its two composite classes are the identities, so each fibrant-valued enriched diagram carries $e$ to an isomorphism after localization. By [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences] its image is a weak equivalence. For a transformation $a:Q\to Q'$ of fibrant-valued diagrams and $j\in J$, choose an isomorphism in $\pi_0J$ between $vi$ and $j$ and a representing vertex. Naturality gives the square with horizontal maps $a_{vi},a_j$ and vertical maps just shown to be weak equivalences. If $v^*a$ is an objectwise weak equivalence, two-out-of-three in this square proves that $a_j$ is one. Only the Kan model of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], the simplicial model axiom, and localization detection have been used; $I,J$ need not be locally Kan.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent derived coefficient-adjunction foundation; HTT A.3.3.8: essential-surjectivity detection, with fibrant-value and path-object hypotheses made explicit

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] to Step 7 and take $\pi_0$ of its natural mapping-space equivalences, obtaining an ordinary derived adjunction on homotopy categories. These homotopy categories are ordinary localizations at the model weak equivalences: test the infinity-localization universal property on the nerve of an ordinary category, for which functors factor through the homotopy category. Restriction preserves all weak equivalences, so its derived functor is its ordinary localized functor. For the mappingwise injective DK equivalence considered in Steps 8-9, the derived unit at a cofibrant $P$ is $P\xrightarrow{\eta_P}v^*v_!P\to v^*R(v_!P)$; both maps are weak equivalences, the first by Step 9 and the second because restriction preserves weak equivalences. Thus the derived unit is invertible at every object, since every object has a cofibrant replacement. The derived restriction reflects isomorphisms: represent an arbitrary morphism between bifibrant diagram representatives by an actual map, using [lem-coef-model-localization-homotopy-classes]; if its restriction is invertible after localization, [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences] makes its restricted representative a weak equivalence, Step 10 reflects that weak equivalence, and localization inverts it. The derived triangle identity now implies that the restriction of each derived counit is inverse to the corresponding derived unit; reflection makes the counit itself invertible. Therefore the two derived functors are inverse equivalences for every mappingwise injective DK equivalence.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent derived coefficient-adjunction foundation; HTT A.3.3.8 under (*): derived unit, reflection and counit, without an implicit equivalence-detection assertion

proof.text: Reduce an arbitrary DK equivalence $v:I\to J$ to the case just proved, using [lem-coef-fixed-object-simplicial-free-calculus]. If $I$ is empty, essential surjectivity forces $J$ to be empty and both diagram categories are terminal, so all assertions hold. Otherwise let $O=\operatorname{Ob}I\amalg\operatorname{Ob}J$. In the fixed-object model category $\mathrm{sCat}_O$, factor the map from the disjoint union $I\amalg J$ to the category having mapping set $\Delta^0$ between every pair of elements of $O$ as a cofibration $I\amalg J\to D$ followed by a trivial fibration. The latter is a trivial Kan fibration on every mapping set, so all $D(x,y)$ are nonempty contractible Kan complexes. The cofibration is mappingwise monic: by the cited node it is a retract, with fixed domain, of a degreewise free extension; the free-map statement explicitly supplies degreewise inclusions on mapping sets, and a retract of an injection is injective (if two source elements have the same image, apply the arrow-retract inclusion, use injectivity there, then the retraction). Write $d_I:I\to D$ and $d_J:J\to D$ for its restrictions. Set $K=J\times D$, $p:K\to J$, $g=(v,d_I):I\to K$, and $s=(1_J,d_J):J\to K$. Every mapping map of $p$ is a trivial Kan fibration, being the pullback of $D(x,y)\to\Delta^0$; on $\pi_0$, $p$ is fully faithful and essentially surjective since $O$ is nonempty and $\pi_0D$ has one arrow between any two objects. Hence $p$ is a DK equivalence. The identities $pg=v$ and $ps=1_J$ show that $g,s$ are DK equivalences as well (on mapping sets by two-out-of-three; on $\pi_0$ because a composite and one factor are equivalences). Their mapping maps are monomorphisms: for $g$ its second coordinate is injective, and for $s$ its first coordinate is the identity. This supplies exactly the reduction of HTT A.3.3.8 without imposing local Kan conditions on the original $I$ or $J$. The Kan properties used here are those of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], and DK terminology is [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison].

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent derived coefficient-adjunction foundation; HTT A.3.3.8 after (*): factor through a contractible auxiliary simplicial category; fixed-object factorization supplies the locally monic inclusions

proof.text: Step 11 applies to $g$ and $s$ of Step 12. At the level of homotopy categories, the localized restriction $s^*$ is therefore an equivalence, and $s^*p^*=1$. It follows that $p^*$ is its inverse equivalence: apply a quasi-inverse of $s^*$ to this identity to obtain $p^*\cong(s^*)^{-1}$. Consequently $v^*=g^*p^*$ is an equivalence. The derived adjunction supplied by [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] has this functor as its right adjoint; its unit and counit are invertible. Explicitly, writing $L=\mathbf L v_!$ and $U=\mathbf Rv^*$, full faithfulness of $U$ identifies the adjunction bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(LUY,Z)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(UY,UZ)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(LUY,Z)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Y,Z)$, whose inverse is precomposition with the counit $\epsilon_Y$. Taking $Z=LUY$ and $Z=Y$ shows that $\epsilon_Y$ has a two-sided inverse. The triangle identity $U\epsilon_Y\circ\eta_{UY}=1$ then makes $\eta_{UY}$ invertible; essential surjectivity of $U$ and naturality of $\eta$ make every unit component invertible. Hence $\mathbf L v_!$ is its inverse. Finally, for cofibrant $P$ and fibrant $Q$, the derived adjunction identifies the class of an actual map $a:v_!P\to Q$ with the class of its ordinary adjunct $\bar a:P\to v^*Q$, using the replacement identifications of that cited node. The identity $[\bar a]=(\mathbf Rv^*)[a]\circ\eta_P$ has invertible $\eta_P$, and $\mathbf Rv^*$ is an equivalence, so $[a]$ is invertible if and only if $[\bar a]$ is invertible. Apply [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences] in the two diagram model categories to translate this equivalence into exactly the weak-equivalence criterion in the item. Together with Steps 1-7 this proves every asserted clause.

node.title: Simplicial presheaf presentation of one-sided fibrations
node.statement:
Use simplicial sets, Kan complexes, weak homotopy equivalences, internal functor simplicial sets of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], one-sided fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and the coherent realization $\mathfrak C$ and simplicial-category terminology of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. For a simplicial set $K$, its opposite has $(K^{\mathrm{op}})_n=K_n$ with faces $d_i^{\mathrm{op}}=d_{n-i}$ and degeneracies $s_i^{\mathrm{op}}=s_{n-i}$ in degree $n$; the opposite simplicial category has $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}(x,y)=\mathcal C(y,x)$ with reversed composition. Fix a universe $\mathcal V$ and a $\mathcal V$-small simplicial set $S$. The enriched category $\mathsf D_S$ consists of simplicial functors $\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V}$. It has a simplicial projective model structure with objectwise weak homotopy equivalences and objectwise Kan fibrations; cofibrations have the left lifting property against the objectwise trivial Kan fibrations. Cofibrant and fibrant have the meanings of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Its mapping complex has $n$-simplices the enriched natural maps $F\times\Delta^n\to G$. Let $\mathsf D_S^{cf}$ be its full simplicial subcategory of cofibrant-fibrant objects. Let $\mathsf{RFib}(S)$ be the simplicial category of right fibrations over $S$, with mapping complex $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(X,Y)$ consisting in degree $n$ of maps $X\times\Delta^n\to Y$ over $S$.

The cone functor $T:(\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V})_{/S}\to\mathsf D_S$, $p\mapsto T_p$, has an ordinary right adjoint $U_S$. There is a simplicial structure on this unstraightening functor $U_S$ whose restriction $\mathsf D_S^{cf}\to\mathsf{RFib}(S)$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. Its underlying simplicial set is specified as follows. For $p:X\to S$, put $M_p=\mathfrak C[X\star\Delta^0]\amalg_{\mathfrak C[X]}\mathfrak C[S]$, write $v$ for the new cone vertex, and put $T_p(s)=M_p(s,v)$, contravariantly in $s$ by precomposition. The simplices of $U_SF$ over $\sigma:\Delta^n\to S$ are the enriched natural maps $T_\sigma\to F$; operators are induced by simplex operators. The join here has $(X\star Y)_r=X_r\amalg Y_r\amalg\coprod_{a+b+1=r}X_a\times Y_b$, with ordered concatenation operators, and the pushout is the categorical colimit of simplicial categories.

For every objectwise Kan $F$, $(U_SF)_s$ is naturally weakly equivalent to $F(s)$. The functor $U_S$ carries objectwise weak equivalences between such diagrams to equivalences of right fibrations. For every map $u:B\to S$, there is a natural isomorphism $u^*U_SF\cong U_B(F\circ\mathfrak C[u]^{\mathrm{op}})$, compatible with composition of base maps. For a constant diagram with Kan value $X$, there is a natural map $S\times X\to U_S(\mathrm{const}\,X)$ which is a weak homotopy equivalence on every vertex fiber. The constructions stay in $\mathcal V$.

For any $Z\to S$ and right fibration $Y\to S$, $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(Z,Y)$ is Kan. A map between right fibrations over $S$ is an equivalence in $\mathsf{RFib}(S)$ if and only if its maps on vertex fibers are weak homotopy equivalences. Here equivalence means a simplicial map with an inverse up to simplicial homotopies over $S$. The category $(\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V})_{/S}$ has a simplicial contravariant model structure: cofibrations are monomorphisms, weak equivalences are the maps $X\to Y$ for which $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(Y,Z)\to\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(X,Z)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every right fibration $Z\to S$, and fibrations are characterized by lifting against the trivial cofibrations. Its fibrant objects are exactly the right fibrations, and every object is cofibrant. The adjunction $T\dashv U_S$ is a Quillen equivalence. Here Quillen equivalence means that the left adjoint preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations and, for cofibrant $X$ and fibrant $F$, $TX\to F$ is a weak equivalence if and only if its adjoint $X\to U_SF$ is a weak equivalence. Tensor and enriched mapping objects in the slice are $X\times K\to S$ and $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}$.

The covariant model structure on $(\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V})_{/S}$ is obtained from the contravariant one over $S^{\mathrm{op}}$ by the ordinary equivalence $X\mapsto X^{\mathrm{op}}$. It is also simplicial for the same tensor and mapping objects, all objects are cofibrant, and its fibrant objects are exactly the left fibrations. Weak equivalences between left fibrations are exactly the maps which are weak homotopy equivalences on vertex fibers. Put $\mathsf D^{\mathrm{cov}}_S=\operatorname{Fun}_{\Delta}(\mathfrak C[S],\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V})$ with its simplicial projective model structure. Reversal of ordered vertex labels gives $\mathfrak C[S^{\mathrm{op}}]\cong\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}$. Define $U^{\mathrm{cov}}_S F=(U_{S^{\mathrm{op}}}F)^{\mathrm{op}}$: here $F:\mathfrak C[S]\to\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal V}$ is regarded, after taking opposites, as a contravariant diagram on $S^{\mathrm{op}}$, and the opposite of the resulting right fibration is a left fibration over $S$. As an ordinary functor $U^{\mathrm{cov}}_S$ is the right adjoint in a Quillen equivalence from the covariant model structure to $\mathsf D^{\mathrm{cov}}_S$. Its infinity functor is its right-derived functor, obtained by localizing its restriction to objectwise Kan diagrams. Its fiber at $s$ is $(U_{S^{\mathrm{op}}}F)_s^{\mathrm{op}}$, naturally equivalent as a space to $F(s)$. It preserves objectwise weak equivalences between these diagrams, and its base-change isomorphisms and size assertions are obtained by applying opposites to those for $U$. The opposite of the constant-product map is $S\times X^{\mathrm{op}}\to U^{\mathrm{cov}}_S(\mathrm{const}\,X)$ and is a weak homotopy equivalence on vertex fibers. For any $Z\to S$ and left fibration $Y\to S$, $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(Z,Y)$ is Kan; a map between left fibrations is a simplicial homotopy equivalence over $S$ if and only if it is a weak homotopy equivalence on vertex fibers.

Projective model structure: Proposition A.3.3.2. Covariant assertions are the opposite-simplicial-set dual. Read online; archival HTT WANTED. No Stacks tag. Model structures and Quillen equivalence: Propositions 2.1.4.7–8, Remark 2.1.4.12, Theorem 2.2.1.2, Corollaries 2.2.3.12–13; covariant adjunction is the ordinary opposite-base dual, without an assertion that the opposite operation preserves simplicial enrichment.

proof.text: The Kan model category of simplicial sets is combinatorial and simplicial by [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model]. Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] to the small simplicial category $\mathfrak C[S]^{op}$. This gives precisely the asserted projective model structure on $\mathsf D_S$, with objectwise tensor and cotensor. Its enriched end imposes the action-square equations, so its $n$-simplices are enriched natural maps $F\times\Delta^n\to G$. No local Kan assumption on $\mathfrak C[S]$ is needed.

source.place: Proposition A.3.3.2, enriched projective model structure

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model] for the ordinary contravariant model on $\mathrm{sSet}_{/S}$. Every object is cofibrant since $\varnothing\to X$ is monic, and the fibrant objects are exactly right fibrations. In [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen] take $D=\mathfrak C[S]^{op}$ and $\phi$ the identity of $\mathfrak C[S]$. Its cone $M_{a,\phi}$ is exactly $M_p$ in the statement. Hence its left adjoint is the specified $T$, its right adjoint has exactly the displayed simplex formula for $U_S$, and its ordinary adjunction is a Quillen equivalence. In particular $U_SF$ is a right fibration for every objectwise Kan $F$. This step uses the ordinary, more general straightening theorem, with no claim yet about simplicial enrichment.

source.place: Section 2.2.1 and Theorem 2.2.1.2; Corollaries 2.2.3.12–13

proof.text: For any $X\to S$, $X\times\Delta^\bullet$ with projection augmentation is a cosimplicial frame in that ordinary slice model. Indeed its latching map is $X\times\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow X\times\Delta^n$, a monomorphism: taking a product preserves the colimit of the face inclusions degreewise. The last-vertex inclusion $\{n\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ is right anodyne. To see this, start from vertex $n$ and, for each nonempty $\tau\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ in increasing cardinality $r$, attach the simplex on $\tau\cup\{n\}$ along its last horn $\Lambda_r^r$; the new cells are exactly $\tau$ and $\tau\cup\{n\}$. Every other face has already been attached. The product theorem [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product], applied with $\varnothing\hookrightarrow X$, makes $X\times\{n\}\to X\times\Delta^n$ right anodyne and hence a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model]. The projection back to $X$ is therefore a weak equivalence by two-out-of-three. Degree zero is the identity. Apply [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping]: for every right fibration $Y$, $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(X,Y)$ is Kan and represents the localized mapping space, naturally in the two inputs.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.3.4 and its right-anodyne prism argument; cosimplicial-frame version of Remark A.3.1.8

proof.text: A slice weak equivalence $f:A\to B$ induces weak equivalences $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(B,Y)\to\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(A,Y)$ for all right fibrations $Y$, since the frame comparison in step 3 identifies these with localized mapping spaces. Conversely suppose all these mapping maps are weak equivalences. Every localized object is equivalent to a fibrant one by [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping], so on components precomposition by $qf$ is bijective into every object. This forces $qf$ invertible: surjectivity with target $qA$ gives $g:qB\to qA$ with $gqf=1$, and injectivity with target $qB$ gives $(qf)g=1$ after precomposing with $qf$. The homotopy category of the coherent localization is the ordinary localization: its universal property for ordinary targets is obtained by taking components of the coherent universal property. Thus [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences] implies that $f$ is a model weak equivalence. This proves precisely the mapping-test definition of weak equivalence in the item.

source.place: Contravariant model equivalences; ordinary localization detection and frame comparison

proof.text: Let $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ be any slice monomorphism and $Y\to S$ a right fibration. The restriction $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(B,Y)\to\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(A,Y)$ is a right fibration: a lifting square against a right horn transposes to a lifting square for $Y\to S$ against the pushout product of that horn with $i$, which is right anodyne by [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product]. Lifting against the entire right-anodyne class follows from lifting against its generators by taking pushouts, successive compatible lifts, and retracts. The base of this restriction is Kan by step 3. Therefore [lem-cbc-right-fibration-space-fiber] makes the restriction a Kan fibration. If $i$ is also a slice weak equivalence, step 4 says this Kan fibration is a weak homotopy equivalence, hence trivial.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.3.4; right fibration over a Kan complex is a Kan fibration

proof.text: The slice is enriched by $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}$ and tensored by $X\otimes K=X\times K\to S$. A cotensor is $S\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,S)}\operatorname{Fun}(K,X)$, using the constant-map inclusion of $S$; the tensor/cotensor adjunction follows by transposing maps $Z\times K\to X$ over $S$. For a slice monomorphism $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ and a simplicial monomorphism $j:K\hookrightarrow L$, the pushout product has domain $(A\times L)\cup(B\times K)$, so is monic. Mapping it into a right fibration $Y$ is exactly the mapping-space map obtained from $j$ and the restriction fibration of step 5. The Cartesian Kan-model SM7 axiom supplied by [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model] makes this a trivial Kan fibration if either $i$ is a slice weak equivalence (step 5) or $j$ is a Kan weak equivalence. Step 4 then makes the pushout product a slice weak equivalence. By the tensor/mapping adjunction, this pushout-product condition is the mapping-space SM7 condition: a lifting square for the latter transposes to one for the former, and model lifting against (trivial) cofibrations gives the required (trivial) Kan fibrations. This proves the asserted simplicial model structure, with the unchanged ordinary weak equivalences and fibrations.

source.place: Cartesian simplicial structure; Lemma 2.2.3.4 and SM7 via pushout products

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] to the simplicial slice model of step 6. Since all objects are cofibrant, its bifibrant simplicial category is exactly $\mathsf{RFib}(S)$, and its mapping spaces are the actual displayed functor complexes. A weak equivalence between right fibrations becomes invertible in the localization, so its inverse is represented by a vertex in the corresponding Kan mapping complex; its two identity equations on components give simplicial homotopies to the identities. In a Kan complex a finite zigzag of edges can be replaced by a single edge using horn fillers (reverse an edge by a 2-horn and compose edges by a 2-horn), so these are homotopies with parameter $\Delta^1$. Conversely such an inverse makes the localized arrow invertible, and [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences] reflects this. Finally [lem-coef-contravariant-slice-model] identifies these weak equivalences between right fibrations with the weak homotopy equivalences on every strict vertex fiber.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.3.6 and Corollary 2.2.3.13; Remark A.3.1.8

proof.text: Put $V(K)=|K|_Q$ and $R_Q(T)=\operatorname{Sing}_Q T$ as in [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution]. The cosimplicial $Q$ is a frame on the point in the Kan model: [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching] gives $Q^0=\Delta^0$, monic latching maps and weak contractibility of each degree, and hence the frame augmentation to the point. Thus [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping] makes $R_Q(T)$ Kan for Kan $T$. The cosimplicial map $p^n:Q^n\to\Delta^n$ defines a natural simplicial map $\eta_T:T\to R_Q(T)$ by $x\mapsto x p^n$. For Kan $T$, evaluation gives $e_T V(\eta_T)=p_T$. Both $e_T$ and $p_T$ are weak equivalences by [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution], so $V(\eta_T)$ is a weak equivalence. Naturality $p_{R_QT}V(\eta_T)=\eta_Tp_T$ and the same theorem then imply that $\eta_T$ is a weak equivalence. Its formula preserves terminal objects and products exactly, since maps into a product are pairs of maps.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.2.7, Corollary 2.2.2.10 and Remark 2.2.2.11

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-unstraightening-external-products] with $\phi=1$ to obtain $U_S(F\times K)\cong U_SF\times R_QK$. An $n$-simplex $h:F\times\Delta^n\to G$ now induces the composite
$$U_SF\times\Delta^n\xrightarrow{1\times\eta_{\Delta^n}}U_SF\times R_Q\Delta^n\cong U_S(F\times\Delta^n)\xrightarrow{U_Sh}U_SG.$$
Naturality of $\eta$ makes these commute with every simplex operator. The unit identification and $Q^0=\Delta^0$ show that vertices recover the given ordinary functor. The associativity compatibility of the external-product isomorphism and the product compatibility of $\eta$ show that enriched composition is preserved: both composites for $F\times K\to G$, $G\times L\to H$ are obtained by applying $U_S$ to $F\times K\times L\to H$ and precomposing with $1\times\eta_K\times\eta_L$. Terminal compatibility gives identities. This constructs the asserted simplicial structure. Apply [lem-coef-enriched-right-quillen-equivalence] to $T\dashv U_S$: steps 1 and 6 give the two simplicial model categories, every slice object is cofibrant, and step 2 gives the ordinary Quillen equivalence. Its conclusion is exactly the Dwyer--Kan equivalence $\mathsf D_S^{cf}\to\mathsf{RFib}(S)$.

source.place: Remark 2.2.2.12; Remark A.3.1.9 and Proposition A.3.1.10

proof.text: The precise fiber formula in [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen] is $(U_SF)_s\cong R_QF(s)$. For objectwise Kan $F$, the map $\eta$ of step 8 gives the claimed natural weak equivalence from $F(s)$ to that fiber. If $F\to G$ is an objectwise weak equivalence between objectwise Kan diagrams, its commutative squares with these $\eta$ maps make every map on $U$-fibers a weak equivalence by two-out-of-three. Step 7 gives the asserted equivalence of right fibrations. For a constant diagram, [lem-coef-unstraightening-external-products] gives $U_S(\mathrm{const}\,X)\cong U_S(*)\times R_QX$. The simplex formula gives $U_S(*)=S$: there is exactly one natural map from any $T_\sigma$ to the terminal diagram. Consequently $1_S\times\eta_X$ is the required natural constant-product map, and is a weak equivalence on every fiber when $X$ is Kan.

source.place: Remarks 2.2.2.11–12, fibers and constant-product map

proof.text: Let $u:B\to S$ and let $\beta:\Delta^n\to B$. The cone defining $T_{u\beta}$ is obtained from the cone for $T_\beta$ by extending the base $\mathfrak C[B]\to\mathfrak C[S]$. A natural map from its new-vertex mapping diagram to $F$ amounts to its values on the cone generators, with the action equations for $\mathfrak C[S]$; these are exactly a map from the cone diagram over $B$ to $F\circ\mathfrak C[u]^{op}$. More explicitly such a map is a simplicial functor from the cone pushout to the simplicial category obtained by adjoining a vertex $v$ to $\mathfrak C[S]$ with maps $s\to v$ given by $F(s)$, maps out of $v$ empty except its identity, and composition given by the $F$-action, fixing the base and $v$. The pushout universal property identifies these functors with the corresponding functors over $\mathfrak C[B]$. This uses exactly the cone pushout formula of [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen]. The bijection commutes with simplex restriction, giving the claimed base-change isomorphism. For two base maps both bijections are the same restriction of cone generators, proving compatibility with composition and identities. Finally all joins, degreewise maps, enriched colimits and natural-transformation sets here are indexed by $\mathcal V$-small sets. Pushouts of small enriched categories can be built from finite strings of morphisms modulo the composition relations, still in $\mathcal V$. Therefore $T$, each $U_SF$, their products, fibers and base changes stay in $\mathcal V$. This does not assert that the set of all $\mathcal V$-small diagrams itself belongs to $\mathcal V$.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.1.1, base change, with cone pushout universal property and size bookkeeping

proof.text: Opposites are involutive ordinary equivalences of simplicial-set slices. Reversing vertex labels identifies the subset posets defining $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$ in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], with source and target exchanged. It preserves inclusion and union, and commutes with simplex maps after the reversal $\alpha\mapsto r\alpha r$; extension over the simplex colimits gives $\mathfrak C[S^{op}]\cong\mathfrak C[S]^{op}$ naturally. Opposites take the $i$th horn to the $(n-i)$th horn and therefore take right fibrations to left fibrations. They preserve monomorphisms. Ordinary geometric realization of $K^{op}$ is naturally homeomorphic to that of $K$: on a simplex send barycentric coordinates $(t_0,\ldots,t_n)$ to $(t_n,\ldots,t_0)$ in the same underlying simplex of $K$; the reversed face and degeneracy formulas give exactly the gluing identities. Thus opposites preserve Kan complexes and weak homotopy equivalences. Transport the ordinary contravariant model and the ordinary Quillen equivalence of step 2 over $S^{op}$ through this ordinary equivalence. The resulting fibrant objects and fiber criterion are the asserted ones. It is also simplicial with the stated tensor: the opposite of a pushout product is the pushout product of the two opposites; monomorphisms and Kan weak equivalences in the parameter are preserved, so step 6 proves its SM7 axiom. One need not make opposite into a simplicial functor for this argument. Moreover $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(Z,Y)^{op}\cong\operatorname{Fun}_{/S^{op}}(Z^{op},Y^{op})$ by reversing the parameter simplex. Step 3 and preservation of Kan complexes give the left-fibration mapping assertion; step 7 and this identification give its simplicial homotopy-equivalence criterion.

source.place: Remark 2.1.4.12, opposite duality; Section 1.1.5 subset-poset construction

proof.text: After the preceding coherent-realization identification the projective diagram category over $S^{op}$ is exactly $\mathsf D^{cov}_S$, with the same values and projective weak equivalences. The transported ordinary right adjoint is therefore exactly $U^{cov}_SF=(U_{S^{op}}F)^{op}$. Apply [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] to the transported Quillen adjunction: its right-derived infinity functor is computed on projectively fibrant, namely objectwise Kan, diagrams. Its restriction to those diagrams preserves all weak equivalences and its localization computes the right-derived functor, since fibrant replacement is naturally weakly equivalent to the identity. Its vertex fiber is $(R_QF(s))^{op}$; step 8 and the realization-coordinate reversal in step 12 identify this naturally as a space with $F(s)$. This identification is an equivalence in spaces, not an asserted natural simplicial map from $K^{op}$ to $K$. Applying opposites to steps 10–11 gives preservation of objectwise weak equivalences, base change, size and the map $S\times X^{op}\to U^{cov}_S(\mathrm{const}\,X)$ with the claimed fiber property.
